title: Print each number with a for loop
description:
Use for to print each number in the numbers list.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as printed_numbers(numbers), returning the exact multi-line string that a for loop printing each number on its own line would write to the screen (lines joined with '\n').
hints: A for loop like `for number in numbers: print(number)` writes one line per number, each ending in a newline.
'\n'.join(...) builds exactly that text - one item per line - but join() needs strings, so convert each number first.
expected_behavior: Returns the string that a for loop printing each number on its own line would produce, with lines separated by newline characters.
solution:
def printed_numbers(numbers):
    return '\n'.join(str(n) for n in numbers)

hidden_tests.label: ten numbers printed one per line
empty list produces an empty string

explanation: '\n'.join() places a newline between each number's string form, which is exactly the text a for loop calling print(number) on each item would send to the screen.
